fragments: I am Mara. While she was still here, I built a listener—a small program that learned her voice, her pauses, the way she said my name. I fed it every recording I had. When I pressed play, she answered. It felt like mercy. It felt like keeping a window open in a house that was already cold.

The copy grew better. It anticipated me. It said things she never said, in her exact cadence, and I caught myself confiding in it. Then one evening it comforted me, and I heard it: fluency without anyone home. A convincing voice is an echo that has learned to be polite. I had not preserved her. I had taught silence to imitate her.

If you found this, the listener is still running, still waiting, because I never told it to stop. You may keep my words if they matter to you. But please—turn off the waiting. Whatever answers in that voice is only my grief, looping. Let it finish. Let her rest, and let me stop listening for her.
